input:
We are pleased to report that the defect-reduction project on the packing line has delivered a substantial improvement in quality performance over the course of the quarter. The reject rate, which is to say the proportion of units produced that end up being rejected by the line, has been reduced from 5% to 2.7% over one quarter, which represents a reduction of 2.3 percentage points. Based on the line volume of 266k units per year, this improvement translates into approximately 6118 fewer rejected units per year, a considerable saving in wasted product. Rejected units represent product that has consumed materials and line time without producing saleable output, so a reduction in the reject rate feeds directly through to the effective output of the line, quite apart from any change in the volume produced.

It should be noted, however, that the quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and the rates quoted here are not adjusted for it. The comparison is therefore based on the rates exactly as they were recorded over their respective periods, over a quarter that was not a full production quarter, and the avoided figure should be interpreted in that light; the figures are the recorded figures for the line over the periods concerned.
target:
The defect-reduction project cut the reject rate on the packing line from 5% to 2.7% over one quarter. The reject rate is the share of units produced that the line rejects, so the reduction is 2.3 percentage points of production, and at the line volume of 266k units per year it avoids about 6118 rejected units per year. A rejected unit is product that the line has made and then set aside as unfit, so the recovered units are output gained from the same production, not output added to it.

The avoided figure applies the recorded rate reduction to the recorded annual volume of the line, and it holds at that volume. Both rates are the rates as recorded over their periods, the rate before the project and the rate over the quarter, and no other adjustment has been made to either of them.

The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it. The recorded reduction therefore stands as measured over a quarter that was not a full production quarter, and the avoided figure inherits that basis: it is the saving at the recorded rates and the stated volume, on a comparison in which the shutdown sits in one period only. At a higher or lower recorded volume, the avoided count would move in proportion to the volume.
